list.name: Server (re)start
list.textFormat: Tutti Frutti server started (deploy, crash or restart)

description: Tutti Frutti server health, gameplay (games, rounds, time-ups), WebSocket connections, persistence (snapshot saves, restore), accounts and Go runtime. Generated by helm/tutti-frutti/dashboards/generate.py: do not edit by hand.

panels.description: UP when Prometheus can scrape the server /metrics endpoint. DOWN also when the target is missing altogether. Check: kubectl -n $namespace get pods; kubectl -n $namespace logs deploy/$job --tail=100.
panels.title: Server

panels.description: Time since the server process started. Drops to zero on every deploy or crash.
panels.title: Uptime

panels.description: Live rooms held in memory (tuttifrutti_rooms). The chart caps them at server.maxRooms.
panels.title: Active rooms

panels.description: Clients attached to a room (joined), tuttifrutti_connections.
panels.title: Connected players

panels.description: Live WebSocket connections, joined or not (tuttifrutti_ws_connections_open). The server refuses upgrades above 2000 (503 server_busy): orange at 1500, red at 1900.
panels.title: Open WebSockets

panels.description: Successful POST /api/rooms (HTTP 201) per minute. Rooms are only created over REST.
panels.title: Rooms created / min

panels.description: Games the host started in the last hour (tuttifrutti_games_started_total; a rematch starts another game and counts again). The Gameplay row shows how they ended.
panels.title: Games started (1 h)

panels.description: Restarts of the server container (crash, OOM kill, failed probe) in 24 h. A normal deploy replaces the pod and is NOT counted. Check: kubectl -n $namespace describe pod -l app.kubernetes.io/component=server (Last State).
panels.title: Container restarts (24 h)

panels.description: Capacity view over time. Sockets above players = connections that have not joined a room yet (join deadline 10 s) or are being replaced. Vertical markers are server (re)starts: deploys and crashes.
panels.title: Rooms, connected players and open sockets

panels.description: Games that reached the final phase in the selected range (tuttifrutti_games_finished_total), by how they ended: completed = every configured round was played, ended_by_host = the host ended it early, letters_exhausted = no letter was left. A game abandoned in the middle (everybody left, idle room) is in none of them.
panels.title: Games finished in range

panels.description: Rounds started in the selected time range (tuttifrutti_rounds_total).
panels.title: Rounds in range

panels.description: Basta calls in the selected time range (tuttifrutti_basta_total). A vote to stop that passes counts as a Basta.
panels.title: Basta calls in range

panels.description: Rounds that ended because the time limit expired (tuttifrutti_time_ups_total) in the selected range. Only games with a time limit have them.
panels.title: Time-ups in range

panels.description: Basta calls / (Basta calls + time-ups) in the selected range: of the rounds that were played to the end, how many a player closed by calling Basta (or by a vote to stop that passed) instead of waiting for the clock. A round that was abandoned counts in neither.
panels.title: Rounds ended by Basta

panels.description: Letters the server picked because the chooser did not tap STOP within 10 s (tuttifrutti_letter_auto_stops_total). Many of them mean players walk away from the phone or the chooser's connection is bad.
panels.title: Letter auto-stops in range

panels.description: Share of client commands answered with an error in the selected range (any result other than ok). Orange above 5 %, red above 20 %: usually a client bug or someone poking the API.
panels.title: Rejected commands

panels.description: Rounds started (tuttifrutti_rounds_total) against the two ways a played round ends: a Basta call (tuttifrutti_basta_total, a passed vote to stop included) or the time limit (tuttifrutti_time_ups_total). Started minus the other two is rounds still running or abandoned.
panels.title: Rounds started, Basta calls and time-ups (per min)

panels.description: Games started (tuttifrutti_games_started_total) and finished by reason (tuttifrutti_games_finished_total). The difference is games in progress or abandoned.
panels.title: Games started and finished (per h)

panels.description: Letters the server picked because the chooser did not tap within 10 s (tuttifrutti_letter_auto_stops_total). Empty means every chooser tapped.
panels.title: Letter auto-stops (per min)

panels.description: Accepted client commands per type (tuttifrutti_commands_total{result="ok"}): what players actually do.
panels.title: Commands by type (per min, accepted)

panels.description: Commands the room refused, by error code: wrong_phase, not_host, invalid_*, rate_limited, server_busy ... Empty means every command was accepted.
panels.title: Rejected commands by result (per min)

panels.description: Rejected / all commands. Dashed lines: 5 % (orange) and 20 % (red).
panels.title: Rejected-command ratio

panels.description: Rejected / all commands of the same type: shows which command misbehaves.

targets.expr: sum by (type) (rate(tuttifrutti_commands_total{namespace="$namespace", job="$job", result!="ok"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (type) (rate(tuttifrutti_commands_total{namespace="$namespace", job="$job"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Rejected-command ratio by type

panels.description: Votes to stop a round (tuttifrutti_stop_votes_total, only in lobbies that enabled them): asked = opened (or passed at once when nobody else was left to ask), then how each ended: passed (the round stopped, counted as a Basta too), declined, timeout (15 s without agreement) or ended (the round moved on, or the asker left). Empty means nobody used the vote.
panels.title: Votes to stop by result (per h)

panels.description: Categories the host asked the AI judge about (tuttifrutti_judge_requests_total, only when the server has Cloudflare credentials): ok = answered, cache_hit = answered from the cache without a call, busy = out of daily budget, rate limit or refused by Cloudflare, error = the call failed or the reply was unusable. Empty means nobody used it.
panels.title: AI judge requests by outcome (per h)

panels.description: Neurons spent today (UTC) by this process (tuttifrutti_judge_neurons_used). The Free plan allows 10000 a day and Cloudflare refuses calls after that; the server stops asking at JUDGE_DAILY_NEURONS (default 9000). It restarts from 0 when the server restarts.
panels.title: AI judge Workers AI Neurons used today

panels.description: GET /ws responses: 101 = connected. 401 missing guest cookie, 403 bad Origin, 429 rate limited / too many connections, 503 server_busy or shutting down.
panels.title: WebSocket upgrades by status (per min)

panels.description: Why connections ended (tuttifrutti_ws_closes_total by close code). 1001/1006 are normal browser churn, 1012 is a deploy, 1008 is the server cutting off a misbehaving or too slow client.

properties.value: 1008 policy (rate limit, queue overflow, join timeout)

panels.title: WebSocket close codes (per min)

panels.description: Upgrades accepted, connections replaced by a newer one of the same player (4001) and abnormal drops (1006). A spike right after a deploy is expected; a constant high churn means flaky networks or a proxy cutting idle sockets.
panels.title: Reconnect churn (per min)

panels.description: HTTP 429 by route. The buckets are shared by all clients (Traefik hides client IPs), so any sustained value means real players are being refused. Empty means healthy.
panels.title: Rate-limited requests (per min)

panels.description: WebSocket frames by direction (tuttifrutti_ws_frames_total). Outbound dominates: every command triggers one state frame per client.
panels.title: Frames in / out (per s)

panels.description: Close code 1008 (tuttifrutti_ws_closes_total): the server cut a client off for exceeding its frame rate, missing the join deadline, sending malformed frames or overflowing its send queue. The red line is exactly the last cause (tuttifrutti_ws_send_drops_total): the client could not keep up with 32 queued frames and reconnects for a fresh snapshot. Occasional drops are phones going through a tunnel; a steady stream means bad networks or a server too slow to write.
panels.title: Policy closes and slow-client drops (per min)

panels.description: Failed room snapshot writes, deletions and janitor sweeps (tuttifrutti_snapshot_errors_total) in the selected range. Anything above zero means Postgres refused or timed out: rooms keep running from memory but would be lost on a restart. Check: kubectl -n $namespace logs deploy/$job | grep -i snapshot.
panels.title: Snapshot errors in range

panels.description: Seconds since the later of the last successful snapshot write (tuttifrutti_snapshot_last_success_timestamp_seconds, 0 until the process has saved once) and the start of the process. It grows while nothing changes: a room that is playing saves every 5 s, an idle one every 90 minutes, so orange (90 min) and red (2 h) are what the TuttiFruttiSnapshotStale alert treats as broken; shorter gaps only matter while snapshots are waiting (panel Snapshot save queue).
panels.title: Time since last successful save

panels.description: Rooms rebuilt from their snapshots when the current server process started (tuttifrutti_rooms_restored_total; the counter only moves during the start). After a deploy this is the number of games that survived it.
panels.title: Rooms restored at last start

panels.description: How long the startup restore took (tuttifrutti_restore_duration_seconds): loading every snapshot and starting its room. The startup probe allows 150 s; orange above 30 s, red above 120 s.
panels.title: Restore duration

panels.description: Saved rooms the current process could not bring back (tuttifrutti_restore_errors_total): unusable snapshots (corrupt, or written by an incompatible version; they are logged and deleted) and snapshots beyond server.maxRooms (left in the store). Check: kubectl -n $namespace logs deploy/$job | grep -i 'snapshot\|not restoring'.
panels.title: Restore errors at last start

panels.description: Snapshots removed from the store in the selected range (tuttifrutti_snapshots_deleted_total): room_closed = a room that ended removed its own (normal), janitor = the hourly sweep removed a row nobody refreshed for 6 h (should stay at 0: live rooms refresh theirs every 90 minutes at the latest).
panels.title: Snapshots deleted in range

panels.description: Room snapshot write attempts (tuttifrutti_snapshot_saves_total): ok, or error = encoding or writing failed (a failed write is retried with backoff, so a database outage shows as a steady stream of errors). Playing rooms save every 5 s, so ok is roughly 12 per playing room per minute.
panels.title: Snapshot saves by result (per min)

panels.description: Failed / all snapshot write attempts. The TuttiFruttiSnapshotSaveFailing alert fires above 50 % (at least 6 attempts in 10 minutes) for 10 minutes; the dashed lines are 20 % (orange) and 50 % (red).
panels.title: Snapshot save error ratio

panels.description: Duration of one snapshot write to Postgres (tuttifrutti_snapshot_save_duration_seconds), successful or not. A healthy database answers in a few milliseconds; the saver gives up on a write after 10 s.
panels.title: Snapshot save latency

panels.description: The Time since last successful save stat over time: a sawtooth that resets at every save. Idle rooms only save every 90 minutes, so teeth of up to 90 minutes are normal; the dashed lines are 15 minutes and 2 hours, the thresholds of the TuttiFruttiSnapshotStale alert (the 15 minute one only counts while snapshots are waiting).
panels.title: Time since the last successful save

panels.description: Rooms whose newest snapshot is waiting for the store, being written or waiting for a retry (tuttifrutti_snapshot_save_queue). It is 0 whenever everything is written: a write takes milliseconds, so a value that stays at 1 or more means the store is failing or hanging (see Snapshot saves by result).
panels.title: Snapshot save queue (rooms waiting)

panels.description: Failed snapshot writes, deletions and janitor sweeps per minute (tuttifrutti_snapshot_errors_total; the writes are also in Snapshot saves by result). A saver retries with backoff (0.2 s to 10 s) so a database outage shows as a steady stream. Empty means healthy.
panels.title: Snapshot errors (per min)

panels.description: Snapshots deleted per hour (tuttifrutti_snapshots_deleted_total): room_closed = rooms that ended, janitor = stale rows swept by the hourly janitor (a janitor line means a snapshot nobody refreshed for 6 hours: investigate).
panels.title: Snapshot deletions by source (per h)

panels.description: kube-state-metrics: the server pod Ready condition. /readyz also pings Postgres, so NOT READY with a healthy process usually means the database is unreachable.
panels.title: Server readiness

panels.description: Kubelet readiness probes (every 5 s): 200 = ready; 503 = shutting down or the database ping failed. A short 503 burst at every deploy is expected.
panels.title: /readyz responses (per min)

panels.description: Server container restarts per interval (kube-state-metrics). Deploys replace the pod and do not count. Check Last State / reason: kubectl -n $namespace describe pod -l app.kubernetes.io/component=server.
panels.title: Container restarts

panels.description: Resets to zero at every deploy or crash; the sawtooth shows when and how often the server restarted.
panels.title: Uptime (time since last start)

panels.description: Google sign-in attempts that reached the callback (tuttifrutti_logins_total): ok, failed (bad state, token exchange or ID token) or cancelled (the user declined). Empty until the first login (or while Google login is not configured).
panels.title: Logins by result (per min)

panels.description: Logins by result in the selected range.
panels.title: Logins in range

panels.description: Lifetime-stats writes at game over (tuttifrutti_stats_recorded_total): ok, error = a failed attempt that is retried, dropped = given up (stats of that game are lost). Failures never block a room. Empty until the first finished game with a logged-in player.
panels.title: Stats recorded by result (per min)

panels.description: Stats writes by result in the selected range.
panels.title: Stats recorded in range

panels.description: Finished games not yet credited to their players' lifetime stats: the recorder queue (tuttifrutti_stats_queue_depth, games waiting for the database writer) and the rooms' outboxes (tuttifrutti_stats_outbox_pending, games the store has not confirmed yet, kept in the room's snapshot). Both are 0 when the database answers; a plateau above 0 means stats writes are failing (see Stats recorded by result and the TuttiFruttiStatsRecordingFailing alert).
panels.title: Stats backlog (finished games waiting)

panels.description: REST and WebSocket-upgrade requests by route pattern, without probes and scrapes.
panels.title: Requests by route (per s)

panels.description: Status classes of all user traffic (101 = WebSocket upgrade).
panels.title: Requests by status code (per s)

panels.description: Server errors / all requests (probes excluded). Dashed line: 5 %. Check: kubectl -n $namespace logs deploy/$job | grep '"status":5'.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(tuttifrutti_http_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", job="$job", route!~"GET /(healthz|readyz|metrics)", code=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / (sum(rate(tuttifrutti_http_requests_total{namespace="$namespace", job="$job", route!~"GET /(healthz|readyz|metrics)"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: 5xx ratio

panels.description: Request latency quantiles from tuttifrutti_http_request_duration_seconds (WebSocket upgrades are excluded: their lifetime is not a latency).
panels.title: Latency (all routes)

panels.description: 95th percentile latency per route pattern.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, route) (rate(tuttifrutti_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace="$namespace", job="$job", route!~"GET /(healthz|readyz|metrics)"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: p95 latency by route

panels.description: go_goroutines. Expect roughly 2 per open socket and 2 per room plus a small constant (~15); steady growth with flat traffic is a goroutine leak.
panels.title: Goroutines

panels.description: Go heap in use, process RSS and the container working set against its memory limit (the pod is OOM-killed at the limit).
panels.title: Memory

panels.description: CPU seconds per second used by the process, against the container CPU request.
panels.title: CPU

panels.description: Garbage-collection cycles per second and the mean pause per cycle.
panels.title: GC

panels.description: Bytes allocated per second (go_memstats_alloc_bytes_total).
panels.title: Allocation rate

panels.description: process_open_fds as a share of the process limit. Each WebSocket uses one.
panels.title: Open file descriptors

title: Tutti Frutti
